title: Frontend: Custom Sort
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Custom Sort. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(records). Return a copied array sorted ascending by numeric priority, then lexicographically by ASCII id. Records have unique string ids and finite numeric priority.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Copy the array and use a comparator that compares priority numerically before applying the chosen secondary comparison.
alternativeApproaches: Accept a list of sort descriptors and define explicit null placement and locale behavior.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Equal priorities; equal secondary keys; negative priority.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
